1.explanation:
All three constants define the regex rules that Highlight.js uses to detect flags and operators in PowerShell code. 

• PS_ARGUMENTS holds the patterns for matching arguments (literal flags) but only matches a single leading hyphen (begin: /(-)[\w\d]+/), so “--flag” is skipped.  
• COMPARISON_OPERATORS is a big alternation of single-hyphen comparison operators (e.g. '-eq', '-gt', etc.); it also omits any double-hyphen form.  
• CMDLETS defines how cmdlet names plus parameters are highlighted (using ‘)+(-)[\w\d]+’), again only matching a single hyphen before the parameter name.  

To support “--flag” syntax, these patterns must be adjusted (e.g. allow /-{1,2}[\w\d]+/ or explicitly include “--” variants).
1.bug_scenario: In the user-provided screenshot and HTML/js setup, a PowerShell code block is highlighted via Highlight.js. The line “foo --bar baz” displays no special styling for “--bar” (the double-hyphen flag), while the single-hyphen “-bar” on the next line is correctly highlighted. In contrast, a native PowerShell 7.1.3 console screenshot shows both “--bar” and “-bar” rendered in yellow, indicating that dual-hyphen flags should be recognized. The discrepancy arises because the current PowerShell grammar in Highlight.js only recognizes single-hyphen operators and parameters.

2.explanation: The PS_ARGUMENTS variant defines how named parameters are highlighted via the regex /(-)[\w\d]+/, which only matches a single leading hyphen. Similarly, the CMDLETS variant uses a pattern that appends '(-)[\w\d]+' to VALID_VERBS, also only capturing one hyphen. To support double-hyphen flags ("--flag"), these two regex patterns must be updated to allow one or two leading hyphens (for example, using /-{1,2}[\w\d]+/). This change will ensure that both single- and double-hyphen parameters are recognized and styled correctly.
2.bug_scenario: In the PowerShell language definition for highlight.js, tokens beginning with a single hyphen (e.g. "-bar") are correctly styled as literals/operators, but tokens beginning with two hyphens (e.g. "--bar") aren’t matched by the regex rules and thus remain unhighlighted. The images show that "--bar" appears plain text while "-bar" is colored.
